The trading week goes smoother when the big decisions are made before it starts.

Here's a 4-step prep you can run before Monday:

1. Check the calendar for scheduled news. Big economic reports can move ES fast, so know which day and what time they hit.
2. Write down your risk limits: stop size, max loss per day, max trades per day.
3. Read last week's journal. Whatever rule you broke most often becomes this week's focus.
4. Pick your trading window. Choose your session and your hours now, not in the moment.

None of it takes long. It means Monday morning opens with your answers already written down.

Decide your loss limit while you're calm, not after a red day.

One ES contract with a 4-point stop puts $200 on the line. Pick a daily max loss, then count how many full stops fit inside it. A $600 max means 3 full stops on 1 contract.

Hit that number and the day is over. The limit stays the same tomorrow.

Write it down before the week starts. Numbers picked mid-week tend to get picked by emotion.

My trading week has a hard edge on both sides.

Monday to Friday I'm at a full-time job, 6:00 AM to 4:30 PM, in a distribution center. Some days I take a trade during lunch, which falls around 10 AM Eastern. Once the break is over, so is my screen time, since phones aren't permitted on the work floor.

The trade review waits until my son's bedtime, once the workday is behind me.

That small window is why my rules stay tight: New York session only, every stop set at 3.5 to 4 points before entry, and 1 or 2 good trades, then done.

Less time on the chart made me more selective, not worse.
